note.text: Read the whole passage before answering. Separate directly stated facts, reasons, proposals and information that remains unknown. An inference needs an identifiable clue and must not turn a fictional case into a universal claim. Notice who speaks and whether a statement is an opinion, a plan or an observed result. This is a written script for listening preparation: no recording is supplied and no hearing or speaking is assessed.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to follow role allocation and a proposed response to a constraint. Builds on: comparing proposals and relevant questions. Leads to: idioms and narrative viewpoints.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original script: A fictional club plans a reading event. Bih volunteers to welcome visitors, Ayuk to arrange the reading order and Manka to prepare signs. The coordinator asks what support each needs. Manka has a timetable clash, so the group proposes sharing sign preparation and confirming the change with her. The coordinator will review tasks before the event. These are volunteers, not an employment-contract case; the event has not happened.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Locate the relevant sentence, state your answer and identify its support. Check whether a question asks what happened, why, or what cannot be concluded. Then use a teacher-provided oral reading for real listening practice if available.
